questions.question: Which helping verb is used with 'I' and 'We' in the traditional Future Indefinite rule?
questions.rationale: Traditionally, 'I' and 'We' take 'shall', while 'You', 'They', 'He', 'She', 'It', and names take 'will'.

questions.question: "When you ___ me, I will help you." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: In an if/when clause referring to the future, use Present Indefinite ('help'), not will/shall — the main clause takes Future Indefinite.

questions.question: What is the structure of Future Continuous Tense?
questions.rationale: Future Continuous Tense follows: Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing, e.g., 'They will not be working without money.'

questions.question: For a Yes/No interrogative future sentence, what is the correct pattern?
options: Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb + Object?
Subject + Helping Verb + Main Verb + Object?
questions.rationale: Closed (Yes/No) interrogative sentences begin with the Helping Verb, followed by Subject + (not) + Main Verb + Object, e.g., 'Is he reading books?'

questions.question: What is the structure of the Future Perfect Tense?
questions.rationale: Future Perfect Tense follows: Subject + will/shall + have + V3, e.g., 'They will have completed their work before we go.'

questions.question: "They ___ their work before we go." Choose the correct form.
questions.rationale: 'Before we go' with a finished action calls for Future Perfect: will/shall + have + V3 — 'will have completed'.

questions.question: Which structure belongs to the Future Perfect Continuous Tense?
options: Subject + will/shall + have been + V1 + ing + from/since + time
questions.rationale: Future Perfect Continuous follows: Subject + will/shall + have been + V1 + ing + from/since + time, e.g., 'They will have been reading Hindi from Monday onwards.'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly applies the conditional clause rule?
options: If they will come here, I will talk to them.
If they come here, I will talk to them.
If they came here, I will talk to them.
When you will help me, I will help you.
questions.rationale: In an if/when clause about two future actions, the if/when clause takes Present Indefinite ('come') and only the main clause takes Future Indefinite.

questions.question: What is the pattern of an open (question word type) interrogative sentence?
options: Question Word + Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb + Object?
Subject + Question Word + Helping Verb + Verb?
Helping Verb + Object + Subject + Question Word?
questions.rationale: Open questions start with a question word (Why, Who, How, Where, When, What), then Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb + Object — e.g., 'When will you come?'

questions.question: "As soon as I ___ New Delhi, I shall send you the file." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: After 'as soon as' (like if/when clauses), use Present Indefinite for the future action; the main clause carries the future tense.
